summary: Well-executed, fully reproducible preregistered autonomous run with comprehensive artifacts. The confirmatory result is a valid null finding for the exact frozen design, but the manuscript contains a critical misstatement in the title and requires explicit, prominent exposition of the shared-generation design choice and its consequence (identical baseline/guarded outputs).
critical_issues: Manuscript title asserts a reduction in misconfiguration ("Reduces LLM NetOps Misconfiguration") that directly contradicts the preregistered experimental outcome (baseline_rate=1.00, guarded_rate=1.00, paired difference=0.00). This is a factual and substantive mislabeling that must be corrected before acceptance.

The experimental design used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (both conditions reused the same generated candidate per pair), a feature that (by design) made baseline and guarded outputs identical and therefore prevented the guarded pipeline from exercising repairs in this run. Although preregistered, this characteristic materially changes the interpretation of the confirmatory test and is not made sufficiently prominent in the manuscript title/abstract/intro; leaving it implicit risks readers drawing unsupported general conclusions about verifier efficacy.
required_revisions: Change the manuscript title to accurately reflect the observed null result for the exact preregistered design (title must not claim that verifier-assisted pipeline reduces misconfiguration).

In the Abstract and at the end of the Introduction, add an explicit single-sentence disclosure that the execution used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (both conditions received the same initial generated candidate per pair), and state briefly that this choice prevented any repair path from being exercised in the guarded condition for this run.

In Methods (Execution semantics) and Results, add a concise, explicit accounting of call counts and the shared-generation effect (e.g., planned_episode_count=400, model_calls_used=200, shared-stage semantics) and a clear statement that no guarded repair calls occurred because the shared initial candidates all passed the oracle; link to the relevant execution_manifest and scoring artifacts (paths/hashes already in the bundle) to support these assertions.

Add a short evidence–claim mapping (one paragraph or compact table, max ~150 words) that ties each principal claim in the Introduction/Contributions to the specific artifact(s) or analysis file(s) supporting it (use provided artifact paths/hashes). This must make it explicit which claims are limited to the exact preregistered design and which (if any) are broader conjectures posed as recommendations or future work.

Remove or rephrase any wording in the Abstract, Introduction, or Conclusion that could be read as generalizing the null result to verifier-assisted pipelines more broadly; replace with properly qualified language that the null finding applies only to the exact frozen design (shared_initial_candidate, single model, deterministic validator, task bank).
optional_revisions: Consider adding an alternative title suggestion that explicitly indicates a null result and the design constraint (e.g., "No Measurable Benefit from Verifier-Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared-Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study").

Expand the Discussion with a brief prescriptive checklist (2–4 bullet points) for future preregistrations that compare guarded vs baseline pipelines (independent generation, repair budget, oracle-coverage tests).

Include one short (≤1 paragraph) example in the main paper showing a representative task manifest entry and its validator trace (task-000001 is present in the artifact bundle) to illustrate why the initial candidate satisfied the oracle.
